hypothesis: Between two points of the torus of revolution the ranking of geodesic routes by length, by heading amplification |j_head(L)| and by focus margin (distance to the first conjugate point) disagree; on a flat torus there are no conjugate points (infinite margin).
input_data: p = (0.0, 0.4), q = (2.0, -0.3) (chart), routes up to length 11.0, extension horizon 8.0
1440-heading fan (convergence rerun at 2880), RK4 batch step 0.025, Newton on (heading, length) with Jacobian [j_head N, v]
mathematical_model: Geodesic + heading Jacobi system on Torus(R=2, r=1), chart (phi, theta); K = cos theta / (r (R + r cos theta)); focus margin = s_c - L for the first zero s_c > 0 of j_head along the extended geodesic (negative: the route passes a conjugate point and is not locally minimizing); targeting condition 1/|j_head(L)|.

title: Add focus-margin-aware route ranking.
uncertainty: Endpoint residual <= 3.1e-07; Wronskian drift <= 5.2e-09; Clairaut drift <= 2.4e-08; batch-vs-transfer amplification difference <= 2.4e-07 (relative); scipy/sympy re-integration: j_head 2.4e-07 (relative), conjugate points 5.6e-07, endpoint 7.4e-09.
unresolved_assumptions: The candidate set is what the fan found up to length 11 and is stable under doubling the density; completeness is not proven.
Focus margin uses conjugate points of p only; conjugate points of q along the reversed route are not separately reported.
Small |j_head(L)| is not robustness: the targeting condition number 1/|j_head(L)| grows as q approaches a conjugate point, and a route with negative focus margin is not locally minimizing.
